trust_decision.summary: On the OAuth/OIDC (and WebAuthn) callback, the sealed state/PKCE/nonce/challenge cookie is accepted if it decrypts with the shared secret and salt=cookie name; nothing ties it to the provider handling the callback, and cookie names are not provider-specific.

landing_point.why: The summary names state/nonce/PKCE check cookies; checks.ts holds sealCookie/parseCookie, the single seal/unseal pair every check goes through.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Redirect-proxy state decode (callback/index.ts:72) only reads a server-generated origin and the real check still runs on the origin deployment's callback, so a solver can argue it is not a check cookie and outside the advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-provider callback must still succeed for state/pkce/nonce and for WebAuthn register/authenticate; providers without a given check skip it (useCookie early return), and OIDC providers whose AS lacks S256 fall back from pkce to nonce at signin. A fix that renames cookies per provider or demands all checks would break config.cookies overrides / these flows.
